abstractions: One form, one selected event and at most two unknown creation receipts stand for the journal and the event list.
formEpoch merges creationDraftEpoch with the form object identity that ownsForm compares; any replacement or close of the form changes it.
The permission request, the option-event readback and note-origin linking are folded into the write step; a failed readback is a lost answer.
The native creation journal (written unknown before the insert, settled to saved by a later read, acknowledged only when saved) lives in the shared calendar plugin and is modeled at its contract.
checkCreations is modeled only while no save runs; the code has no such guard, and the check only reads and acknowledges saved receipts.
A remount stands for a new component instance: the latch and the receipt view are instance state, the journal is durable.
Two events and revisions up to 2. The inspected content (title, body, location, instants) is one revision number.
One awaited inspection or source preparation at a time; an older one is already retired by the epoch, so dropping it loses nothing.
The Android fallback from inspect to inspectDeletion is one inspection step.
Cap and OpCap of 2 stand for the 32-row creation history and the 100-row operation store; byte limits are not modeled.
Rows are counted, not identified: pending rows split into those a readback will find and those with no saved reminder.
Field-by-field matching of a saved reminder against its request is one found/not-found answer.

ownerDiscard is defined and exercised by scenarios but is not part of step: the Android reminder screens have no action that removes an unconfirmed record. The unresolvable states are reachability witnesses.
Edit, cancel, complete and snooze share one operation record shape and one flow.
Up to three taps; native keeps the newest pending token, so an earlier unconsumed one is replaced.
blocked merges a hidden page, an open connection chooser, a sensitive context and an open Calendar form.
The reminder list read and the target comparison are one listed/not-listed answer; the reviewed question is consume or release.
Native token storage and its own recheck of source, occurrence and revision are modeled as "consume only the current token".
Device rows and the reminder store are version numbers; up to five refreshes.
Reconciling creation and operation intents inside a refresh is covered by ReminderIntents and is part of the refresh succeeding or failing here.
A change to reminders starts a refresh in the same step (the committed and document-changed events).
Request fields (action, time, label, repeat days, time zone) are one review identity; a time-zone change counts as retiring the review.
Mock simulation and the blocked no-connection path exist only in test-mock builds and are not modeled.
The history store is one record with a compare-and-exchange save; the legacy localStorage copy is not modeled.
A handoff is never replayed from history: the model has no action that reads a record and dispatches.
Two pages. The set of posted alarms is a version number; a changed set rings again.
allowed merges visibility, the development background flag, mock mode and the screen lock.
The one-second poll and the 60-second sound limit are nondeterministic steps; elapsed time is not counted.
This is the browser double of the Clock app; the Android handoff is ClockHandoff.
Three consecutive days, one event and one form. Offsets are whole days; hours, zones and DST are not modeled.
Google rows compute their offset at each render and are always current, so only device and reminder rows are modeled.
refreshDue stands for the interval between local midnight and the timer or resume that follows it.
A plain form has no retained identity (a new reminder, or an edit of an unsent Google create): neither draft adapter re-anchors it. That shift is a reachability witness, not an invariant.
Two identities plus signed out, two ranges, one saved read. Calendar preferences are part of the request key and are not varied.
Only the newest read is tracked: an older one is aborted and its continuation returns at its first current() check.
Per-account and per-calendar partial failures collapse into ready, unavailable, lost and error.
The five-minute age of a saved read is a boolean that a nondeterministic step clears.
The outbox and its paused-delete offers are modeled in CalendarSync and CalendarOutboxScheduling.
One linked row, two contexts and local revisions up to 3; the 2,000-event limit is not modeled.
The reconciler is shared upstream code: its outcome is a nondeterministic value from the report keys.
A write whose answer is dropped because sync was paused meanwhile is left quarantined; that is the contract assumed of the upstream dispatch journal.
init starts with the saved opt-in either on or off, since the preference outlives a session.
Two views and at most four lifetimes; queued changes are a counter and each send is one step.
Retry back-off, the Undo-window wake and the stale-holder wake are one timer that is set whenever something is queued.

A request that waits behind a stopped send runs under the lifetime that was live when it arrived. google-calendar-outbox.ts resolves the lifetime when the waiting request starts instead; see the verification notes.
Which change is claimed and how its outcome settles are modeled in CalendarSync.

stateMapping.phase/kind/holder/instance/sending: GoogleCalendarOutboxOp phase, the durable holder, and sendingId (the change this instance is sending now)
stateMapping.undoOpen/hasDeadline/clockKnown/wasPause: the delete deadline and its monotonic window, the pause when the clock cannot time it, the Undo offered again by Calendar and how the pause ended
stateMapping.baseRevision/remoteRevision/checked/remo: read-before-write on the content revision, an event missing from the days read, the owner keeping a change to an unseen event, and Google answering gone
stateMapping.unknown/ownRemote: a lost answer to an update, reply or delete, and Google already showing what that send set (googleCalendarChangeApplied)
stateMapping.failure/writable/restorePermission: Google refusing the check read or the write for want of permission, the failed change, and retryPermission after a reconnect shows the grant
stateMapping.retryAuthorized/applied/sends/created/tw: uncertain create matching by title, start and end against ids recorded before the send, explicit retry and write outcome
stateMapping.consent/localRevision/consentReview: reviewed linked-sync preference and exact current context

abstractions: One outbox entry, two revisions, two holders and at most two sends expose interference without the full event collection.
checking splits the durable dispatching phase into preflight and actual network dispatch. Restarts map both back to source recovery states.

Time is not modeled: retry back-off (retryAt), the wait before another holder's unfinished send is taken back (DISPATCH_STALE_MS) and the abort of a running send when the last view detaches are abstractions. Detach and single-flight sending are in CalendarOutboxScheduling.
Recurring-event scope, timestamp parsing, merging multiple queued edits and upstream linked reconciler internals remain abstractions checked by runtime contracts.

Unknown creates allow an explicit retry after owner review. The model does not claim globally exactly-once Calendar creates, and a lookalike event the loaded feed did not show before the send can still be adopted (UnseenTwinAdoptedWitness).
checkUnreadable keeps the lost-answer marker across a failed check read. In google-calendar-outbox.ts settle() replaces the error, so the marker is lost there; see the verification notes.

Permission restoration is an authorized current-account readback. It queues again only a change that failed for want of permission and preserves operation owner, request epoch, unknown-create state and linked-sync consent.
Calendar offers Undo again for a paused delete only while Calendar is shown; resolvePaused is reachable only through that offer.

stateMapping.view/day/month/search/menu/deleteSheet/c: Calendar persistent view choice and Back order: the shell lowers the conversation, then form, delete sheet, event, menu, search
stateMapping.generation/desiredRange/requestRange/req: latest-wins desired-range loading: a forced read supersedes the one in flight, and only the newest read publishes or ends loading
stateMapping.owner/hidden/googleRowsOwner/localAccess: owner-scoped Google preferences, access as last read here against the provider grant, and the saved read that may be shown before the accounts are read again
stateMapping.form/formDay/formTarget/formOwner/openOw: civil-date draft recovery, retained creation identity, immutable save snapshot, a confirmed save, and Google surfaces closed when their account leaves

abstractions: Two source identities (device event and Google event), two account identities, day/month offsets -1..1 and up to five read-generation changes.
Date arithmetic, DST resolution, recurrence expansion and visual grid geometry remain pure implementation contracts; this model tracks transitions and retained identities across those calculations.
Calendar writes are modeled in CalendarSync and CalendarDeviceWrites. This module tracks presentation/read/draft state and never gives a restored form provider authority.
Cached rows may remain while a broader/narrower range is loading. Committed-result freshness and owner isolation are checked independently of cache presentation.
The device read and the Google read share one request/reply pair; the Google reader's own epochs are in GoogleCalendarReader.
The guest picker inside a form (form.pq), which Back closes before the form, is not modeled.
A grant withdrawn outside the app is learned at the next read of the accounts; the five-minute age of the saved read is a boolean.

stateMapping.running/epoch/starts: admitAndStart synchronized decision/start and surrounding lifecycle ownership
stateMapping.deferred/failedStarts: an admitted start the service refuses (RuntimeException caught in ResidentScheduleReceiver), deferred to a later broadcast or foreground launch

abstractions: Five broadcast classes, three lifecycle generations, three actual process starts and two refused starts.
Decision and start are atomic under the same lock, matching admitAndStart. A canary shows the forbidden split-admission interleaving.
First-unlock state differs from screen lock. Occurrence execution and occurrence recovery belong to the shared runtime and are not modeled here.
foregroundLaunch stands for the app starting an admissible resident when it is next opened.
Historical current/proposed design comparison at source ef9fbf7cd7, not a runtime conformance claim.
All original state variables are fields of s; immutable Design selects behavior; record spreads preserve the original frame conditions.
Finite domains and numeric constants are unchanged from the original model configuration.
Persistent history booleans monitor the original action properties without restricting transitions; TLC checks the equivalent invariants and temporal monitor formulas.
Keep mine after Google reports the event gone: the design model keeps the change, the runtime drops it whatever the choice. CalendarSync (goneAnswer, GoneOnlyDrops) models the runtime.
RSVP is enabled in the design model and capability-gated off in the runtime until Cloud supports it.
One Undo slot: several deletes with their own Undo windows, which the runtime allows, are outside this model and covered per operation by CalendarSync.
OutboxDrains holds for the design model under its fairness assumptions only. The runtime phases paused, uncertain and failed leave only by an owner action and are not in this model.

readme.modeledState: phase/kind/holder/sending, deadline/pause/offer/decision, base and remote revision with missing and gone events, lost answers and own writes, permission failure and retry, uncertain create matching, linked-sync consent
identity, request key, read epoch, saved read shown first, rows bound to the identity they were read for, Connect offered when no account grants Calendar
one serialized operation, exact-review enable, opt-in checked around each provider request, row states clean/dirty/conflicted/quarantined/paused
attached views and their lifetime, the single running send, a request waiting behind a stopped send, the wake timer

Selected month/day, shell-then-view Back order, latest-wins read tokens, confirmed save and the day it shows, visible calendars, known access against the provider grant, Google surfaces closed when their account leaves
Creation receipts (unknown, saved, acknowledged), explicit separate creation, the single write in progress, superseded forms, the unconfirmed-write latch and its clearing read, inspect-then-delete
The inspected open event or prepared calendar source exposed to the assistant, retired by an epoch on every read, close and new form
Creation records pending/found within a bounded history, operation records until a succeeded receipt, read-only recovery, and the records nothing can resolve
Native pending tap token, one check at a time with a queued explicit request, interaction fence, consume only after the exact detail is shown
Newest refresh publishes, device rows published even when the reminder store fails, stale marking, navigation intent kept until a successful refresh
Review identity, view and history generations, durable opening/result record, retired review never handed off, no replay
Two pages, one lock holder that owns and rings, release when hidden or nothing rings, sound limited per ring
Today, row offsets and the day they were read, the midnight refresh, re-anchoring of retained forms, forms with no retained identity
Ordered admission decision, lifecycle lock, starts, and an admitted start the service refuses and defers
